description.narrative:
1. The intervention approach/methodology/instruments API's approach combines capacity-building, digital tool development and maintenance, structured citizen–council dialogue, and policy engagement, building directly on API's existing digital platforms (Citizen Budget App, PIDOR Chatbot) and its long-standing sub-national networks in Kampong Thom, Pursat, and Phnom Penh. Consistent with API's lessons learned, activities pair training with follow-up coaching and mentoring rather than one-off sessions, andcombine digital engagement with offline, face-to-face dialogue. As a cross-cutting method, API will produce educational and awareness content across multiple social media channels (Facebook, Telegram, YouTube, Website) — including short explainer videos,posters, citizen-story and info posts, live Q<(>&<)>A sessions, and podcast/audio segments — and will facilitate online social dialogues that connect citizens with local authorities and link back to the Citizen Budget App and PIDOR Chatbot, ensuring digital outreach complements offline forumsand reaches youth and harder-to-reach groups. API's activities follow the consortium activities matrix submitted to SDC; the activity codes below correspond to that matrix.
Outcome 1: Capacity and Participation Strategic intervention: API will build the capacityof citizens and responsive local authorities by combining structured capacity-building, institutional strengthening, and digital engagement — simultaneously increasing citizen capability, institutional readiness, and access to information.
Outcome 2: Accountability and Oversight Strategic intervention: API will operationalise accountability by shifting trained citizens from passive participants to active leaders of oversight and advocacy processes, throughcitizen initiatives that generate evidence and engage directly with government platforms, and by embedding civic engagement culture among youth through schools.
Outcome 3: Institutionalisation and Sustainability Strategic intervention: API will support the transition from project-driven engagement to system-level institutionalisation of participatory governance, ensuring participation-related policies and practices are revised, tested, and implemented to promote effective civic participation in localbudget and fiscal management.
2. Target Groups API's target groups reflect the consortium-wide analysis, applied specifically to API's three target provinces: Kampong Thom, Pursat, and Phnom Penh. CBOs. CBOs play an important bridging role between citizens and local authorities, but many still have limited technical capacity in planning, budgeting, and follow-up on accountability actions. Women members of CBOs face additional barriers related to time poverty, domestic responsibilities, and lower confidence speaking in public. API will strengthen CBO capacity through training, coaching, and practical engagement in citizen awareness-raising, monitoring, and community-level consultation, with intentional support for women's active representation and leadership within CBOs. Commune and district councillors/staff. Commune and district councils are the closest elected authority to citizens, yet awareness among sub-national officials on PFM and community concerns remains low. API will provide training, mentoring, and practical tools on civic engagement, inclusive facilitation, and gender-responsive budgeting, and support commune- and district-level dialogue between citizens and CBOs. Commune councillors/staff, district councillors/officials, and provincial officials will participate as key duty-bearers in training, dialogue, budget transparency, expenditure oversight, procurement accountability, and institutionalization of citizen engagement approaches. Provincial councillors/officials. Provincial-level actors play an important coordination and oversight role but are often more removed from direct citizen engagement. API will engage provincial actorsthrough dialogue, evidence-sharing, and selected capacity support linked to sub-national accountability and local planning responsiveness. Youth (15–30). Youth are a major share of Cambodia's population, but their participation in local planning and budgeting remains low (see Section 1.1). API will provide youth-focused civic engagement training, awareness-raising, and digital and offline participation opportunities, with intentional support for young women and marginalised youth, including youth with disabilities. Youth will participate as citizen monitors, community representatives, and active participants inPFM awareness, local budget monitoring, dialogue, and accountability processes, especially around CIP, DIP, expenditure, and procurement oversight. Women: Women will participate as citizens, CBO members, community representatives, and local monitors. Theproject will promote women’s voice and leadership in budget transparency, expenditure oversight, procurement monitoring, and local dialogue. Indigenous peoples. Indigenous communitiesare explicitly identified in I-SAF and DMK guidance as groups requiring inclusive outreach. API will promote culturally and linguistically accessible outreach and facilitation for indigenous communities in target areas, with gender-sensitive engagement to ensure indigenous women are actively included. Indigenous participants in API target areas will be engaged in awareness raising, consultation, and accountability processes to ensure their priorities are reflected in local budgeting and expenditure discussions. Persons with disabilities (target ~5%). Persons with disabilities remain significantly underrepresented in social accountability processes. API will apply disability-inclusive facilitation and participation measures in awareness-raising, meetings, training, and monitoring activities, informed by API's 2021 disability-inclusion research. Persons with disabilities will be supported to participate in accessible and inclusive PFM awareness, monitoring, and dialogue activities, including citizen oversight and local accountability processes. Teachers / Students: Teachersand students will participate as key multipliers and youth civic actors in the project. Teachers will strengthen their knowledge and facilitation capacity on civic engagement, governance, social service budgeting, public procurement, gender-responsive budgeting, and digital participation, and will help guide and mentor student-led civic initiatives. Students will participate as young civic actors and learners, building practical knowledge and skills on local governance, budgeting, social accountability,debate, and project management so they can engage in youth-led initiatives and participate more actively in local governance and public finance processes. Older people (60+, target ~20%). Older people hold valuable knowledge of local history and communitypriorities but may face mobility, literacy, and digital-confidence barriers. API will ensure awareness-raising, meetings, and dialogue processes use accessible communication methods and mixed-age participation arrangements.

participating-org.narrative:
On May 24th, 2007, Advocacy and Policy Program (APP) made an important step in this localization process by adopting its new name, the Advocacy and Policy Institute (API) in order to reflect its fledgling independent identity. A further important step was taken on July 17th, 2007, when API officially registered with the Royal Government of Cambodia's (RGC) Ministry of Interior as a non-profit, non-governmental organization. API#s goal is #to increase Cambodia#s democratic space by creating more effectiveadvocates and responsive government institutions.# API#s vision is #a Cambodian nation that through poverty reduction and the protection of human rights creates a national culture of harmony with sustainable democratic, political, and economic stability.#API#s mission is #to serve the long term democratic and social development needs of Cambodia through the empowerment of people to interact with their government to protect their rights and provide for their needs.#
API#s Values: All Cambodians have theright to participate, mobilise and express themselves in matters that affect their daily lives. All matters should be resolved peacefully and justly according to the principles of our shared humanity. Building capacity, particularly at the community level, is the most sustainable way of building a brighter future for all Cambodians. Engaging with all social sectors ensures that when solutions are reached, they are of greatest benefit to the community. Being transparent, accountable, independent, and non-partisan helps build an organisation that has the respectand confidence of both the Cambodian people and its international supporters.
